Performance Review Policy

Purpose
The company uses a structured performance review process to align individual contributions with business goals, support development, recognize impact, and address performance concerns early. Reviews are designed to be fair, evidence-based, and consistent across functions including customer operations, fulfillment, merchandising, and technology.

Review Cycle
Formal reviews occur twice each year, with a mid-year check-in and an annual review. New employees hired within 60 days of a cycle may receive a modified review focused on ramp progress rather than a full performance rating. In addition to formal reviews, managers are expected to provide regular coaching throughout the year. Performance conversations should not be saved only for review season.

Evaluation Criteria
Employees are assessed on role outcomes, quality standards, collaboration, accountability, customer impact where relevant, and alignment with company values. Managers must use objective evidence such as metric performance, project outcomes, quality audits, escalation handling, process improvement contributions, and documented feedback. Ratings may not be based on recency bias, personal preference, schedule flexibility unrelated to role needs, or protected characteristics.

Review Process
HR publishes the cycle calendar, templates, and calibration deadlines at least 30 days in advance. Employees complete a self-review by the assigned deadline. Managers then draft the review, citing evidence for each major assessment point and proposing a performance rating. Department leaders participate in calibration discussions to improve consistency across teams. HR reviews submitted ratings for pattern risks, policy adherence, and potential bias indicators before reviews are finalized. Managers deliver the final review in a live conversation and document employee acknowledgment in the performance system.

Development Planning
Every review must include at least two forward-looking development actions. These may include skill building, scope expansion, training, mentorship, or process ownership goals. Employees rated as meeting or exceeding expectations should still receive stretch development guidance. Employees who need improvement must receive a written action plan with measurable expectations, support resources, and follow-up dates.

Link to Compensation and Promotion
Performance reviews may inform merit increases, bonus decisions, and promotion consideration, but they do not automatically guarantee any employment action. Compensation and promotion decisions also consider budget, organizational need, internal equity, readiness for next-level scope, and sustained performance over time. Managers should never promise a compensation outcome before the formal approval process is complete.

Disputes and Corrections
Employees who believe a review contains factual errors or materially incomplete information may submit a written request for reconsideration within 10 business days. HR will review the request with the manager and next-level leader. If a correction is warranted, the updated review must clearly state what changed and why. Disagreement alone does not require a rating change.

Manager Expectations and Compliance
Managers must complete required reviewer training before submitting ratings. Missing deadlines, incomplete evidence, or repeated bias concerns may result in escalation to senior leadership. HR monitors review completion, rating distribution, and follow-through on development plans to ensure the process remains credible and useful.

Recordkeeping
Completed reviews, calibration notes, and formal development plans must be retained in the approved performance system. HR may audit selected records to confirm that ratings align with documented evidence and that required follow-up conversations occurred.
